_readme: All the words of The Pitch live here. Change any sentence between quotes and keep the quotes, commas and brackets as they are. 'roast' is Alice at level 5, 'soft' is the gentle setting, 'clean' is the no-swearing version. Where a line has an 'fr' part, that is the French translation shown underneath during the first steps. 'celebrations' are the punchy lines Alice shouts, one at random, every time the learner gets it right. Each lesson in 'lessons' follows the 5 steps: hook, three phrases, your turn (replies: good true/false), feedback (fix, brilliant, traps) and send-off. 'situation' is the room it belongs to.

welcome.roast: I'm Alice. I've sat through a thousand meetings so you don't have to suffer through one more in silence. Ready?
welcome.soft: I'm Alice. I'll help you speak up in English meetings, one small step at a time.

fr.roast: Moi, c'est Alice. J'ai survécu à mille réunions pour que vous n'en subissiez plus une seule en silence. Prêt·e ?
fr.soft: Moi, c'est Alice. Je vais vous aider à prendre la parole en réunion en anglais, petit à petit.

comeback.roast: When the shit hits the fan, some guys run and some guys stay… glad you decided to stay.
comeback.clean: When things get tough, some people run and some people stay… glad you decided to stay.
comeback.soft: Welcome back! Lovely to see you. Shall we do five minutes?

fr.roast: Quand ça part en vrille, certains fuient et d'autres restent… contente que vous soyez resté·e.
fr.clean: Quand ça se corse, certains fuient et d'autres restent… contente que vous soyez resté·e.
fr.soft: Bon retour ! Ravie de vous revoir. On fait cinq minutes ?

meeting.roast: You apologised three times in one sentence last week. You're not British, you don't get the discount.
meeting.soft: Breathe, smile, and remember: they want to hear what you think.

fr.roast: La semaine dernière, vous vous êtes excusé·e trois fois dans une seule phrase. Vous n'êtes pas britannique, vous n'avez pas droit à la réduction.
fr.soft: Respirez, souriez, et rappelez-vous : ils veulent savoir ce que vous pensez.

settings.roast: Turn me down if you must. I'll still be thinking it.
settings.soft: No problem, I'll be gentle. Mostly.

fr.roast: Baissez-moi le son si vous voulez. Je n'en penserai pas moins.
fr.soft: Pas de souci, je serai douce. Enfin, presque.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: Your shoes aren't going to pitch for you, darling. We start with Survive. Lots of it.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: Totally normal. We'll start with ready-made phrases that get you through.

fr.roast: Vos chaussures ne vont pas pitcher à votre place, chéri·e. On commence par Survive. Beaucoup de Survive.
fr.soft: C'est tout à fait normal. On commence par des phrases toutes prêtes pour vous en sortir.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: Translating in your head again? I can hear the gears from here. We'll speed you up.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: You understand more than you think. Let's get you speaking sooner.

fr.roast: Encore en train de traduire dans votre tête ? J'entends les rouages d'ici. On va accélérer tout ça.
fr.soft: Vous comprenez plus que vous ne le pensez. On va vous faire parler plus tôt.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: So you're fluent, just… beige. Let's give you some personality in English.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: Great base. Now let's make your English sound like you.

fr.roast: Donc vous parlez anglais, mais… en beige. On va donner un peu de personnalité à votre anglais.
fr.soft: Belle base. Maintenant, faisons en sorte que votre anglais vous ressemble.

situations: Ask for budget, time or help
Write an email that gets a reply

ask: Frame it so the answer is yes
nego: Hold your number with a smile
chair: Keep it on time, bring quiet people in
network: Make a contact who calls you back
deliver: Spot the problem and get it on paper, politely

phraseBank: Nice to meet you, I'm in charge of…
Sorry, could you say that again?
Let me get back to you on that.

phrases: I see where you're coming from, but the results speak for themselves.
Let me explain why this matters for the team.
Could we look at what we'd lose if we cut it?

attack.brad: Honestly? Nobody needs this. Let's cut it and move on.
attack.boss: Hmm. I'm not sure. Maybe. Let's see. What do you think, quickly?

replies: bad
OK, no problem, we can cut it.
You folded faster than a deckchair. Stand your ground, darling.
Too quick to give up. You can push back politely.
Vous vous êtes plié·e plus vite qu'une chaise longue. Tenez bon, chéri·e.
Vous cédez trop vite. Vous pouvez contester poliment.
fr
I am not agree, it is very important.
“I am not agree.” The Marseillaise again. It's “I don't agree”.
Nearly! It's “I don't agree”, no “am”.
« I am not agree. » Encore La Marseillaise. On dit « I don't agree ».
Presque ! C'est « I don't agree », sans « am ».
good
I see where you're coming from, but the results speak for themselves. Let me show you.
Look at you. Brad just sat down and said nothing. A first.
Perfect: calm, clear and convincing.
Regardez-vous. Brad vient de se rasseoir sans un mot. Une première.
Parfait : calme, clair et convaincant.

phrases: I understand, and here's why the number makes sense.
If we can agree on the timing, I can be flexible on the details.
I'd rather find something that works for both of us.

attack.brad: That's way too much. Give me twenty percent off or we're done.
attack.boss: It feels… expensive? Can you do something? Whatever you think.

replies: bad
Sorry, sorry, OK, twenty percent.
You just gave away twenty percent and an apology. Hold your number with a smile.
Don't give in straight away. Hold your number.
Vous venez de lâcher vingt pour cent et une excuse. Tenez votre prix avec le sourire.
Ne cédez pas tout de suite. Tenez votre prix.
fr
I can make an effort on the price, it is possible.
“Make an effort” is very French. In English: “I can be flexible on…”.
Try “I can be flexible on…” instead.
« Make an effort », c'est très français. En anglais : « I can be flexible on… ».
Essayez plutôt « I can be flexible on… ».
good
I understand. If we can agree on the timing, I can be flexible on the details.
Oh, that's a negotiator. Brad is now Googling you.
Excellent. You stayed firm and friendly.
Ça, c'est de la négociation. Brad est en train de vous googler.
Excellent. Ferme et aimable à la fois.

phrases: I'll keep this short: three points.
The key thing to remember is this.
Happy to take questions at the end.

attack.brad: Can you just get to the point? I've got another call in five.
attack.boss: So… what's the… you know, the main thing? In one sentence?

replies: bad
Euh, yes, sorry, so, euh, I will explain everything…
That “euh” lasted longer than my last relationship. Breathe, then speak.
Take a breath before you start. Fewer “euh”.
Ce « euh » a duré plus longtemps que ma dernière relation. Respirez, puis parlez.
Respirez avant de commencer. Moins de « euh ».
fr
Actually, I will present you the planning.
“Actually” means “en fait”, not “actuellement”. And it's “the schedule”.
Careful: “actually” means “en fait”. And say “the schedule”.
« Actually » veut dire « en fait », pas « actuellement ». Et on dit « the schedule ».
Attention : « actually » veut dire « en fait ». Et dites « the schedule ».
good
Of course. Three points, two minutes. The key thing is this:
Short, sharp, in control. Brad's other call can wait.
Great: short, clear and confident.
Court, précis, maîtrisé. L'autre appel de Brad peut attendre.
Très bien : court, clair et assuré.

lessons.title: Disagree politely

hook.roast: Saying “No, that's wrong” in a meeting is how you get fewer meetings. Let's fix that.
hook.soft: Saying “No, that's wrong” can sound harsh in English. Let's find a smoother way.

fr.roast: Dire « No, that's wrong » en réunion, c'est le meilleur moyen d'avoir moins de réunions. On arrange ça.
fr.soft: Dire « No, that's wrong » peut sembler brutal en anglais. Trouvons une façon plus douce.

lessons.hookFr: Aujourd'hui : être en désaccord sans claquer la porte.

phrases.say: I see where you're coming from, but…
phrases.fr: Je comprends votre point de vue, mais…

phrases.say: I'm not sure that's the best option.
phrases.fr: Je ne suis pas sûr·e que ce soit la meilleure option.

phrases.html: Could we look at it from another angle?
phrases.say: Could we look at it from another angle?
phrases.fr: Et si on regardait ça sous un autre angle ?

lessons.tip: Le piège français : on dit I agree, jamais « I am agree ».

character.name: Brad · New York
character.line: Let's just cut the training budget. Nobody uses it anyway.

replies.text: No, that's wrong.
replies.roast: Brilliant. Brad now hates you and the budget is still cut. Softer, darling. Try again.
replies.soft: A bit direct for a meeting. Try a softer way in.
replies.fix: Soften before you push back: “I see where you're coming from, but…”

fr.roast: Bravo. Brad vous déteste et le budget est quand même coupé. Plus en douceur, chéri·e. Encore.
fr.soft: Un peu direct pour une réunion. Essayez une entrée en matière plus douce.

replies.text: I am not agree with you.
replies.roast: “I am not agree.” The whole meeting just heard the Marseillaise. It's “I don't agree”. Again.
replies.soft: Nearly! In English it's “I don't agree”, no “am”. Try again.
replies.fix: It's “I don't agree”, never “I am not agree”.

fr.roast: « I am not agree. » Toute la réunion vient d'entendre La Marseillaise. On dit « I don't agree ». Encore.
fr.soft: Presque ! En anglais, c'est « I don't agree », sans « am ». Réessayez.

replies.text: I see where you're coming from, but the numbers tell a different story.
replies.roast: Oh, look at you. That sentence would get you a second meeting and someone else's parking space.
replies.soft: Perfect. Polite, clear and confident.

fr.roast: Regardez-moi ça. Avec cette phrase, vous décrochez une deuxième réunion et la place de parking de quelqu'un d'autre.
fr.soft: Parfait. Poli, clair et sûr de vous.

lessons.noFix: Nothing to fix. Annoying, frankly. Next time, add a reason: “…because the numbers show…”
lessons.brilliant: Your stress on “but” was perfect. Brad felt that.
lessons.endTitle: You just disagreed with someone in English and nobody died.

sendoff.roast: Same time tomorrow? I'll bring the coffee. You bring the confidence.

fr.roast: Même heure demain ? J'apporte le café. Vous apportez l'assurance.
fr.soft: Beau travail. À demain ?

newPhrases: I see where you're coming from, but…
I'm not sure that's the best option.
Could we look at it from another angle?

lessons.title: Move a meeting

hook.roast: Ask an English colleague to “advance the meeting” and they'll think you want to promote it. Today we move meetings like a pro.
hook.soft: Today: how to move a meeting in English, without the false friends.

fr.roast: Demandez à un collègue anglais d'« advance the meeting » et il croira que vous voulez la promouvoir. Aujourd'hui, on déplace les réunions comme des pros.
fr.soft: Aujourd'hui : déplacer une réunion en anglais, sans les faux amis.

lessons.hookFr: Aujourd'hui : avancer, reporter ou déplacer une réunion, sans faux amis.

phrases.html: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?
phrases.say: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?

phrases.html: Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?
phrases.say: Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?

phrases.html: Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
phrases.say: Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
phrases.fr: Changer de salle (ou : « switch to Teams »)

lessons.tip: Pour finir, vérifiez toujours : Does that still work for you?

character.name: Brad · New York
character.line: Hey, bad news. I'm stuck in Lyon. I have to stay here until Thursday, so we need to move Tuesday's meeting.

replies.text: Oh no! So you rest in Lyon until Thursday?
replies.roast: “Rest”? Brad isn't having a nap in Lyon, darling. Rester is stay. To rest is se reposer. Brad has to stay.
replies.soft: Careful: “rester” is “to stay”. “To rest” means “se reposer”.
replies.fix: Rester = to stay. To rest = se reposer.

fr.roast: « Rest » ? Brad ne fait pas la sieste à Lyon, chéri·e. Rester, c'est stay. To rest, c'est se reposer. Brad doit rester.
fr.soft: Attention : « rester » se dit « to stay ». « To rest » veut dire « se reposer ».

replies.text: No problem, we can retard the meeting to Thursday.
replies.roast: “Retard” is an insult in English, darling. Brad is now on the phone to HR. It's “push back”.
replies.clean: “Retard” is a very rude word in English. Brad's eyebrows just hit the ceiling. It's “push back”.
replies.soft: Avoid “retard”: it's offensive in English. Say “push back”.
replies.fix: Reporter = push it back. Never “retard”.

fr.roast: « Retard » est une insulte en anglais, chéri·e. Brad est au téléphone avec les RH. On dit « push back ».
fr.clean: « Retard » est un mot très grossier en anglais. Les sourcils de Brad ont touché le plafond. On dit « push back ».
fr.soft: Évitez « retard » : c'est offensant en anglais. Dites « push back ».

replies.text: Can we advance it to Monday?
replies.roast: “Advance” it? It's a meeting, not a soldier. It's “bring forward”. Also, Brad has to stay in Lyon until Thursday. Keep up.
replies.soft: Avancer = “bring forward”. And Brad can't come before Thursday.
replies.fix: Avancer = bring it forward, not “advance”.

fr.roast: « Advance » ? C'est une réunion, pas un soldat. On dit « bring forward ». Et Brad doit rester à Lyon jusqu'à jeudi. Suivez un peu.
fr.soft: Avancer = « bring forward ». Et Brad ne peut pas venir avant jeudi.

replies.text: No problem. Shall we push it back to Thursday at ten, and do it on Teams in case you're running late?
replies.roast: New time, new venue, one sentence. Brad's assistant wants your number.
replies.soft: Perfect: new time, new place, clear and friendly.

fr.roast: Nouvelle heure, nouveau lieu, une seule phrase. L'assistante de Brad veut votre numéro.
fr.soft: Parfait : nouvelle heure, nouveau lieu, clair et sympathique.

lessons.noFix: Nothing to fix. Show-off. Next time, finish with “Does that still work for you?”
lessons.brilliant: New time and new venue in one sentence. That's how you run a call.
lessons.endTitle: You just moved a meeting without moving a muscle in your face.

sendoff.roast: Same time tomorrow? Or shall we push it back?

fr.roast: Même heure demain ? Ou on la reporte ?
fr.soft: Bravo. À demain ?

newPhrases: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?
Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?
Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
I have to stay until Thursday.
Does that still work for you?

lessons.title: Take a delivery

hook.roast: A driver in a hurry, a pen in your face, and “just sign here, love”. Sign without checking and those crushed boxes are now your problem. Today you check first, in English.
hook.soft: Today: how to take a delivery in English, and check it before you sign.

fr.roast: Un livreur pressé, un stylo sous le nez et « signez là ». Signez sans vérifier, et les cartons écrasés deviennent votre problème. Aujourd'hui, on vérifie d'abord, en anglais.
fr.soft: Aujourd'hui : recevoir une livraison en anglais, et vérifier avant de signer.

lessons.hookFr: Aujourd'hui : recevoir une livraison, vérifier, et signer avec réserves.

phrases.html: Could you bring it round to the loading bay?
phrases.say: Could you bring it round to the loading bay?
phrases.fr: Pouvez-vous passer par le quai de livraison ?

phrases.html: Hang on, I'll just check it before I sign.
phrases.say: Hang on, I'll just check it before I sign.
phrases.fr: Attendez, je vérifie avant de signer.

phrases.say: I'm signing for it as damaged.

lessons.tip: Bonus : We were expecting twelve, but there are only ten. Can you note that on the delivery note?

character.name: Gary · le livreur
character.line: Alright? Delivery for The Pitch. Twelve boxes. Sign here, would you? I'm on a double yellow.
character.note: Vous comptez dix cartons, et l'un d'eux est écrasé.

replies.text: OK, I sign.
replies.roast: Congratulations. You just signed for twelve boxes you didn't get and one you can't use. Gary's gone. So is your refund.
replies.soft: Careful: never sign before you check. Two boxes are missing and one is damaged.
replies.fix: Check first: Hang on, I'll just check it before I sign.

fr.roast: Félicitations. Vous venez de signer pour douze cartons que vous n'avez pas reçus, dont un inutilisable. Gary est parti. Votre remboursement aussi.
fr.soft: Attention : ne signez jamais avant de vérifier. Il manque deux cartons et un est abîmé.

replies.text: Wait, I must control the goods.
replies.roast: Control them? They're boxes, not toddlers. It's “check the goods”. Gary thinks you're about to arrest the parcels.
replies.soft: Contrôler = “check”. Say “I'll just check the goods”.
replies.fix: Contrôler la marchandise = check the goods.

fr.roast: Les contrôler ? Ce sont des cartons, pas des enfants. On dit « check the goods ». Gary croit que vous allez arrêter les colis.
fr.soft: Contrôler = « check ». Dites « I'll just check the goods ».

replies.text: I sign with reserves, this colis is broken.
replies.roast: Reserves? Gary thinks you're booking a table for two. You “sign for it as damaged”. And a colis is a parcel or a box.
replies.soft: Signer avec réserves = “sign for it as damaged”. Un colis = “a parcel” or “a box”.
replies.fix: Signer avec réserves = sign for it as damaged. Colis = parcel, box.

fr.roast: Des réserves ? Gary croit que vous réservez une table pour deux. On dit « sign for it as damaged ». Et un colis, c'est « a parcel » ou « a box ».
fr.soft: Signer avec réserves = « sign for it as damaged ». Un colis = « a parcel » ou « a box ».

replies.text: Hang on, I'll just check it first. There are only ten boxes, not twelve, and this one's damaged, so I'm signing for it as damaged. Can you note that on the delivery note?
replies.roast: Polite, firm, and Gary's double yellow is not your problem. Accounts will build you a statue.
replies.soft: Perfect: you checked, you named the problem, and you got it on paper.

fr.roast: Poli, ferme, et la place interdite de Gary n'est pas votre problème. La compta va vous élever une statue.
fr.soft: Parfait : vous avez vérifié, nommé le problème, et tout est écrit.

lessons.noFix: Nothing to fix. Gary is impressed and slightly scared.
lessons.brilliant: You checked, you counted, and you got it on the delivery note. That's how you take a delivery.
lessons.endTitle: You just stopped a man on a double yellow from rushing you.

sendoff.roast: Honestly? That's leadership. Same time tomorrow.

fr.roast: Franchement ? C'est ça, le leadership. À demain, même heure.
fr.soft: Bravo. À demain ?

newPhrases: Hang on, I'll just check it before I sign.
I'm signing for it as damaged.
Can you note that on the delivery note?
Could you bring it round to the loading bay?
We were expecting twelve, but there are only ten.

lessons.title: Wrong site, wrong pallets

hook.roast: The pallets are off the lorry, they're in your car park, and they're not even yours. Today you say no to a man with a forklift, nicely.
hook.soft: Today: a delivery has arrived at the wrong site. You say no, politely.

fr.roast: Les palettes sont déchargées, elles sont sur votre parking, et elles ne sont même pas à vous. Aujourd'hui, vous dites non à un homme avec un chariot élévateur, poliment.
fr.soft: Aujourd'hui : une livraison arrive sur le mauvais site. Vous dites non, poliment.

lessons.hookFr: Le bon de livraison indique Castres. Vous êtes à Mazamet.

character.name: Gary · le livreur
character.note: Le bon de livraison indique Castres. Vous êtes à Mazamet.

traps: I'm afraid I can't accept it
I'm going to have to ask you to…
it might save you time next time if we…

levels.name: Survive

phrases.html: I'm afraid this delivery is for our Castres site.
phrases.say: I'm afraid this delivery is for our Castres site.
phrases.fr: Je crains que cette livraison soit pour notre site de Castres.

phrases.html: I can't sign for it, I'm afraid.
phrases.say: I can't sign for it, I'm afraid.

phrases.html: Could you load it back on, please?
phrases.say: Could you load it back on, please?

exchanges.line: Right, that's six pallets off. Sign here, love. I've got four more drops before lunch.

replies.text: OK, leave them here, we will manage.
replies.roast: Lovely. Six pallets of someone else's stuff in your car park, and you just volunteered to drive them to Castres. Hope you like forklifts.
replies.soft: Careful: if you keep them, getting them to Castres becomes your job.

fr.roast: Parfait. Six palettes qui ne sont pas à vous sur votre parking, et vous venez de vous porter volontaire pour les livrer à Castres. J'espère que vous aimez les chariots élévateurs.
fr.soft: Attention : si vous les gardez, les livrer à Castres devient votre travail.

replies.fix: Don't keep them: Could you load it back on, please?

replies.text: You must recharge the pallets.
replies.roast: Recharge them? They're pallets, not phones. It's “load them back on”, or “reload” them.
replies.soft: Recharger = “reload” or “load them back on”. “Recharge” is for batteries.

fr.roast: Les recharger ? Ce sont des palettes, pas des téléphones. On dit « load them back on » ou « reload » them.
fr.soft: Recharger = « reload » ou « load them back on ». « Recharge », c'est pour les batteries.

replies.fix: Recharger = reload, load it back on.

replies.text: Sorry, this delivery is for our Castres site, so I can't sign for it. Could you load it back on, please?
replies.roast: Clear, polite, and no signature. You survived Gary.
replies.soft: Perfect: clear, polite, and no signature.

fr.roast: Clair, poli, et sans signature. Vous avez survécu à Gary.
fr.soft: Parfait : clair, poli, et sans signature.

levels.noFix: Nothing to fix. Next level, Gary argues back.
levels.brilliant: You said no without signing and without a fight.
levels.endTitle: You said no to a man with a forklift.

sendoff.soft: Well done. Next level: Gary argues back.

fr.roast: La prochaine fois, il répond.
fr.soft: Bravo. Niveau suivant : Gary répond.

newPhrases: I'm afraid this delivery is for our other site.
I can't sign for it, I'm afraid.
Could you load it back on, please?

levels.name: Handle

phrases.fr: Je comprends tout à fait, mais…

phrases.html: If I sign, they're ours, and they're not.
phrases.say: If I sign, they're ours, and they're not.
phrases.fr: Si je signe, elles sont à nous, et ce n'est pas le cas.

phrases.html: I'm going to have to ask you to load them back on.
phrases.say: I'm going to have to ask you to load them back on.
phrases.fr: Je vais devoir vous demander de les recharger.

exchanges.line: Right, that's six pallets off. Sign here, love. I've got four more drops before lunch.

replies.text: It's not my problem, you made a fault.
replies.roast: A fault? Gary isn't playing tennis. It's “there's been a mistake”. And “not my problem” just made Gary park his lorry across your entrance.
replies.soft: Say “there's been a mistake”, not “a fault”. And “not my problem” sounds rude.

fr.roast: Une faute ? Gary ne joue pas au tennis. On dit « there's been a mistake ». Et « not my problem » vient de pousser Gary à garer son camion devant votre entrée.
fr.soft: Dites « there's been a mistake », pas « a fault ». Et « not my problem » sonne impoli.

replies.fix: Une erreur = a mistake: “there's been a mistake”. Never “it's not my problem”.

replies.text: OK, I sign, but it's not correct.
replies.roast: Once you sign, they're yours. “But it's not correct” won't help you in front of Accounts.
replies.soft: Careful: once you sign, the goods are yours. Don't sign for the wrong delivery.

fr.roast: Une fois signé, elles sont à vous. « But it's not correct » ne vous sauvera pas face à la compta.
fr.soft: Attention : une fois signé, la marchandise est à vous. Ne signez pas une mauvaise livraison.

replies.fix: Don't sign: I can't sign for it, I'm afraid.

replies.text: I'm sorry, I know you're busy, but this is for our Castres site, so I can't sign for it.
replies.roast: Sympathy first, then the facts. Brace yourself, he's not done.
replies.soft: Good: sympathy first, then the facts. He's going to push back.

fr.roast: D'abord de l'empathie, ensuite les faits. Accrochez-vous, il n'a pas fini.
fr.soft: Bien : l'empathie d'abord, puis les faits. Il va insister.

exchanges.line: I'm not reloading that lot, love. Took me twenty minutes to get it off. Just sign and your lot can sort it out.

replies.text: OK, no problem.
replies.roast: Gary pushed once and you folded like a deckchair. Hold your ground.
replies.soft: Don't give in at the first push. Hold your ground, politely.

fr.roast: Gary a poussé une fois et vous vous êtes plié comme une chaise longue. Tenez bon.
fr.soft: Ne cédez pas à la première objection. Tenez bon, poliment.

replies.fix: Hold your ground: I completely understand, but…

replies.text: You must! It's obligatory!
replies.roast: Obligatory? You sound like a parking fine. And shouting makes Gary slower, not faster.
replies.soft: “Obligatory” sounds harsh. Try “I'm going to have to ask you to…”.

fr.roast: Obligatoire ? On dirait une amende de stationnement. Et crier rend Gary plus lent, pas plus rapide.
fr.soft: « Obligatory » sonne dur. Essayez « I'm going to have to ask you to… ».

replies.fix: C'est obligatoire = I'm going to have to ask you to…

replies.text: I completely understand, and I'm sorry about the extra work. But if I sign, they're ours, and they're not. I'm going to have to ask you to load them back on.
replies.roast: Sympathy, reason, request. Gary sighs, but the forklift's moving.
replies.soft: Perfect: sympathy, a reason, then a clear request.

fr.roast: Empathie, raison, demande. Gary soupire, mais le chariot avance.
fr.soft: Parfait : de l'empathie, une raison, puis une demande claire.

levels.noFix: Nothing to fix. Gary sighed, you didn't budge.
levels.brilliant: Sympathy, a reason, then the request. That's how you hold your ground.
levels.endTitle: He pushed, you didn't budge, and nobody shouted.

fr.roast: Prêt pour le niveau final ?
fr.soft: Bravo. Prêt pour le niveau 3 ?

newPhrases: If I sign, they're ours, and they're not.
I'm going to have to ask you to load them back on.

levels.name: Own it

phrases.html: You may well be right about that, but…
phrases.say: You may well be right about that, but…
Shall we call your office together?

phrases.html: It might save you time next time if we…
phrases.say: It might save you time next time if we…
phrases.fr: Cela vous ferait peut-être gagner du temps la prochaine fois si on…

exchanges.line: Right, that's six pallets off. Sign here, love. I've got four more drops before lunch.

replies.text: It's not my problem, you made a fault.
replies.roast: A fault? Gary isn't playing tennis. It's “there's been a mistake”. And “not my problem” just made Gary park his lorry across your entrance.
replies.soft: Say “there's been a mistake”, not “a fault”. And “not my problem” sounds rude.

fr.roast: Une faute ? Gary ne joue pas au tennis. On dit « there's been a mistake ». Et « not my problem » vient de pousser Gary à garer son camion devant votre entrée.
fr.soft: Dites « there's been a mistake », pas « a fault ». Et « not my problem » sonne impoli.

replies.fix: Une erreur = a mistake: “there's been a mistake”. Never “it's not my problem”.

replies.text: OK, I sign, but it's not correct.
replies.roast: Once you sign, they're yours. “But it's not correct” won't help you in front of Accounts.
replies.soft: Careful: once you sign, the goods are yours. Don't sign for the wrong delivery.

fr.roast: Une fois signé, elles sont à vous. « But it's not correct » ne vous sauvera pas face à la compta.
fr.soft: Attention : une fois signé, la marchandise est à vous. Ne signez pas une mauvaise livraison.

replies.fix: Don't sign: I can't sign for it, I'm afraid.

replies.text: I'm sorry, I know you're busy, but this is for our Castres site, so I can't sign for it.
replies.roast: Sympathy first, then the facts. Brace yourself, he's not done.
replies.soft: Good: sympathy first, then the facts. He's going to push back.

fr.roast: D'abord de l'empathie, ensuite les faits. Accrochez-vous, il n'a pas fini.
fr.soft: Bien : l'empathie d'abord, puis les faits. Il va insister.

exchanges.line: Look, it's your lot who gave us the address. Not my fault. Just sign and ring your office.

replies.text: No, it's your fault, you didn't check.
replies.roast: Maybe true, and now Gary's parked across your gate out of spite. Being right isn't the same as winning.
replies.soft: Blaming him makes things worse. Agree with what's true, then hold your line.

fr.roast: C'est peut-être vrai, et maintenant Gary bloque votre portail par dépit. Avoir raison, ce n'est pas gagner.
fr.soft: Le blâmer aggrave les choses. Admettez ce qui est vrai, puis tenez bon.

replies.fix: Don't blame: You may well be right about that, but…

replies.text: Yes, you're right, sorry, I'll sign.
replies.roast: He blamed you and you apologised for existing. Nope.
replies.soft: Don't apologise and give in. You can agree with part of it and still not sign.

fr.roast: Il vous a accusé et vous vous êtes excusé d'exister. Non.
fr.soft: Ne vous excusez pas en cédant. Vous pouvez lui donner en partie raison sans signer.

replies.fix: Agree in part, then hold firm: …but I can't sign for goods that aren't ours.

replies.text: You may well be right about the address, and I'll check that with our office. But I can't sign for goods that aren't ours. Shall we call your office now and sort it out together?
replies.roast: Agree with the part that's true, hold the line on the rest, offer a solution. That's objection handling, darling.
replies.soft: Perfect: you agreed with what's true, held firm, and offered a solution.

fr.roast: Admettre ce qui est vrai, tenir bon sur le reste, proposer une solution. Ça, c'est gérer une objection.
fr.soft: Parfait : vous avez admis ce qui est vrai, tenu bon et proposé une solution.

exchanges.line: Right, the office says reload and take it to Castres. That's my whole morning gone.
exchanges.note: Après l'appel. Gary n'est pas content.

replies.text: Next time, read the delivery note before you unload.
replies.roast: Correct, and he'll remember it forever. As a reason to deliver your stuff last.
replies.soft: True, but it sounds like a telling-off. Try “It might save you time next time if we…”.

fr.roast: Exact, et il s'en souviendra toute sa vie. Comme raison de vous livrer en dernier.
fr.soft: Vrai, mais ça sonne comme un reproche. Essayez « It might save you time next time if we… ».

replies.fix: Vous auriez dû… = It might save you time next time if we…

replies.text: Sorry, sorry, it's all our fault.
replies.roast: It isn't, and now everyone thinks it is. Be positive but don't grovel.
replies.soft: It wasn't your fault. Stay positive without over-apologising.

fr.roast: Ce n'est pas le cas, et maintenant tout le monde le croit. Soyez positif, mais ne rampez pas.
fr.soft: Ce n'était pas votre faute. Restez positif sans trop vous excuser.

replies.fix: Thank him instead: Thanks so much for sorting it.

replies.text: Thanks so much for sorting it, Gary, I really appreciate it. It might save you time next time if we check the site name together before you unload. Have a good rest of the day.
replies.roast: You just told a man he got it wrong, and he thanked you for it. That's owning the room. Or the car park.
replies.soft: Perfect: thanks first, then tactful feedback in positive language.

fr.roast: Vous venez de dire à un homme qu'il s'est trompé, et il vous a remercié. Ça, c'est maîtriser la salle. Ou le parking.
fr.soft: Parfait : d'abord un merci, puis un retour plein de tact, en langage positif.

levels.noFix: Nothing to fix. Gary will deliver to you first from now on.
levels.brilliant: You gave feedback in positive language: “It might save you time next time if we…”.
levels.endTitle: You sent six pallets back to Castres and Gary still likes you.

fr.roast: À demain.
fr.soft: Excellent travail. À demain.

newPhrases: You may well be right about that, but…
Shall we call your office together?
It might save you time next time if we…
Thanks so much for sorting it, I really appreciate it.
